questions.stem: In an exhumed body which of the following poisons can be detected in bones:
questions.solutionHtml:
Arsenic

Arsenic gets deposited preferentially in Bones, Hairs and Nails .Thus even if the body has been buried or burnt after death Arsenic can still be detected in the remnant bones.

To detect chronic arsenic poisoning blood is not a good sample as all the minute amounts of arsenic introduced into the body for a long time has selectively deposited in the bones.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 132,538.

questions.stem: A witness comes to court for evidence recording. Witness is giving false evidence in court of law. This offense is punishable under which IPC?
questions.solutionHtml:
193
  • Perjury-the act of telling a lie in a court of law is punishable under S. 193 IPC.
  • Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; and whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any other case, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 13.

questions.stemHtml: In a dead body having, bloated face and tongue protruding out the following (shown in the picture) was noted. What is the probable cause of the finding seen in the picture?
questions.solutionHtml:
Putrefaction

The findings that can be seen in the picture are skin blebs and greenish discoloration of the body.These are post-mortem changes due to Putrefaction.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 164.

questions.stem: The Onus of proof in civil negligence case against a doctor lies with:
questions.solutionHtml:
Patient

Onus of proof- liability to prove the allegation and it commonly lies on the party who is alleging the charges.In Civil negligence plaintiff is a patient while defender is Doctor. Thus the onus lies upon the patient.

Patient has to prove the allegations through evidence.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 35.

questions.stem: Magnan’s symptoms are associated with which poisoning event?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cocaine

Magnan's symptom is seen in people with cocaine addiction who experience Paraesthesia which feels like a constantly moving foreign body, such as fine sand or powder, under the skin. The sign is named after Valentin Magnan,This is also known cocaine bug as addicted person feel insect is crawling under the skin.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 603.

questions.stem: Most commonly used drug which leads to drug dependence?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cannabis
  • Addictions of drugs are as follows -
  • Nicotine > Alcohol > Cannabis > Painkillers > Cocaine > Heroin > Benzodiazepines  
  • Most commonly used drug among the options is cannabis.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number-604,605 .

questions.stem: In a rape incident on small child the hymen?

options.label: B
options.text: Rupture, because it is situated superficially

options.label: C
options.text: Don’t rupture because it is thick

options.label: D
options.text: Don’t rupture because it is situated deeply

questions.answerText: Don’t rupture because it is situated deeply
questions.solutionHtml:
Don’t rupture because it is situated deeply

The hymen is a thin piece of mucosal tissue that surrounds or partially covers the external vaginal opening .In child the hymen is situated deeply and it is of mostly crescent shaped and due to gross difference in the sizes of the external genitalia of the small victim and the rape offender, often the male penis is not pushed deep into the vagina and thus the Hymen remains intact.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 421.

questions.stemHtml: The POCSO act defines a child as a person under the age of 18 years. However this definition is a purely biological one and does not take into account people who live with intellectual and psycho-social disability. As per POCSO act, a child was brought for age estimation. X ray wrist was taken. The age of this wrist joint is:
questions.solutionHtml:
10 years
  • Pisiform has appeared and seen in the X-ray which is suggestive of  9-12yr age.
  • Union of shaft of 1st metacarpal with its head occurs at 15 yr of age
  • In the context of this question it has not fused. Thus the finding suggests that the age is < 15 years.
  • So taking the criteria of pisiform bone and 1st metatarsal shaft not fused with its base the best answer is 10 years.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 75.

questions.stemHtml: An investigation team reached a crime site where the team collects the trace evidences and send it to the forensic laboratory, where a forensic expert see “Yellow colour needle shape crystals” in microscopy. What is the test?
questions.solutionHtml:
Barberios test

Among the above given options only Barberios test shows Yellow color needle shape crystals.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 434.

questions.stem: Tattoo marks are not visible during autopsy as confirmed by relatives, they alleges that it has been removed artificially by someone. Where tattooing or pigment used in the tattooing can be checked next during autopsy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Regional Lymph nodes

Tattoo marks are designs made by multiple small puncture wounds made through the dermis layer with needles or similar penetrating tools dipped in coloring agents (dye) . which are drained into nearby lymph nodes via subcutaneous lymphatics.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 92.
